description: The bar chart illustrates the popularity scores of various large language models (LLMs) and evaluation conditions across three distinct categories: “Songs,” “Basketball,” and an unlabeled leftmost group (likely representing a baseline or control). The vertical axis, labeled “Popularity,” ranges from 60 to 220 in increments of 20, with a linear scale. The horizontal axis displays the three categories, each containing six grouped bars representing different models or conditions: Llama3 (solid blue), Qwen2 (solid red), ChatGPT (solid yellow), Acc=0 & GT Ans (blue with diagonal stripes), Acc=0 & Gene Ans (red with diagonal stripes), and Acc=1 & GT Ans (yellow with diagonal stripes), as indicated by the legend in the upper left. In the “Songs” category, popularity scores range from approximately 65 (Llama3, Acc=0 & GT Ans) to 140 (ChatGPT, Acc=1 & GT Ans). In the “Basketball” category, scores are substantially higher, ranging from about 160 (Qwen2, Acc=0 & GT Ans) to over 220 (ChatGPT, Acc=1 & GT Ans). The leftmost group shows the lowest scores across all models and conditions, with values generally between 60 and 80. Across all categories, the “Acc=1 & GT Ans” condition consistently yields the highest popularity scores for each model, followed by “Acc=0 & Gene Ans,” while “Acc=0 & GT Ans” typically shows the lowest scores within each model group. The bars are arranged in fixed groupings per category, with no sorting by value, and no bars are visually emphasized beyond their color and pattern coding.
